claims.text: The LORD rejects Samuel’s outward estimate, says that he sees the heart, identifies David, and the spirit comes on David after Samuel anoints him.
In the cave David restrains himself and his men; from Jerusalem the king sees, asks, sends, and takes through servants.
The house oracle promises offspring, throne, discipline, and steadfast love; later narrative places announced consequence and rebellion inside David’s household.

Samuel frames the census with the LORD’s anger and reports one set of totals; Chronicles names Satan and reports another set while preserving the shared command, objection, guilt, plague, and intercession.
Later sources variously select command fidelity, Uriah, worship, warfare, heart and will, ancestry, witness, victory, and suffering.
Jesus presents the relation as an unanswered Temple question; Peter later distinguishes David’s tomb and applies David’s enthronement saying to the risen Jesus.
Revelation announces the Root of David before showing a slain-standing Lamb, then closes with Jesus naming himself David’s root and offspring.
